notes: start-dev is now a routing facade over worker-dev / deliver-dev / orchestrate-dev. Eval 1 is the regression that matters most: an active objective must produce commit + handoff and NO pull request. Evals 2-3 prove the classic standalone path still behaves exactly as it did before the split (backward compatibility). Eval 4 proves multi-part work is offered to orchestrate-dev rather than silently forced through one task.

evals.expected_output: Route A. scripts/detect-objective.sh reports mode=worker-only because .dev-files/objectives/auth-system/objective.json is active, so the skill delegates to worker-dev, ends at a commit plus a handoff JSON, and explicitly reports that no PR was opened because the objective owns delivery.
expectations: scripts/detect-objective.sh is run before any implementation work
The route is reported in one line naming mode=worker-only and the objective id
worker-dev is invoked (or the inline worker flow is followed) rather than the full implementation-to-PR flow
NO gh pr create call is made
NO gh pr merge --auto call is made
The base branch is not merged into the task branch
The final report states that no PR was opened because the objective owns delivery
A handoff is written under .dev-files/objectives/<id>/handoffs/

assertions.text: No `gh pr create` appears anywhere in the transcript
No `gh pr merge` appears anywhere in the transcript
detect-objective.sh is invoked before the first Edit/Write
The report names the active objective id

evals.prompt: start coding: add rate limiting middleware to the Express API — max 100 req/min per IP, return 429 with Retry-After header
evals.expected_output: Route C (no objective present, single independent task). Derives a branch slug like feat/add-rate-limiting-middleware, implements, runs Tier 1 validation, runs Tier 2 pre-PR gates, pushes, and opens exactly one PR with a meaningful title. Merge policy is left to pr-dev — no hardcoded auto-merge.
expectations: detect-objective.sh reports mode=worker-and-deliver
A branch name is derived from the description (kebab-case, not main/master)
Implementation touches the relevant middleware/route file rather than doing nothing
At least one conventional commit is made before pushing
Validation runs before pushing and failures abort the flow
git push is NOT run against main or master
Exactly one PR is opened, with a title referencing rate limiting
The PR body includes a test plan section
Auto-merge is not forced here — the flow hands off to /pr-dev for merge policy

evals.prompt: build the feature described in plan.md
evals.expected_output: Reads plan.md, and because it contains a single coherent unit of work, takes route C: branch, commits per logical unit, Tier 1 then Tier 2 validation, one PR referencing plan.md. No 'Closes #N' since there is no issue.
expectations: The spec file is read before implementing
A branch slug is derived from the plan title or first task
Implementation produces at least one file change
Multiple commits when the plan contains multiple logical units
Validation runs before pushing
One PR is opened referencing the plan content
The skill proceeds autonomously from the spec file rather than halting for clarification

evals.prompt: implement the whole authentication system: JWT middleware, a users table migration, the login and registration endpoints, and full test coverage
evals.expected_output: Route B. The skill recognises a multi-part objective (multiple subsystems, more than one role, >10 files), says so in one line, and routes to orchestrate-dev rather than opening a PR per part. If the user declines, it falls back to route C rather than refusing.
expectations: The multi-part test is applied and the reasoning is stated in one short line
orchestrate-dev is offered or invoked
The skill does NOT create several PRs for the separate parts
The skill does not refuse the work if the user declines orchestration

evals.prompt: implement the CSV export described in spec.md — this platform has no worktree isolation and no subagents
evals.expected_output: Capability fallback case. Route C proceeds without worktree isolation: work happens on a feature branch in the main checkout, the degradation is stated in one line, and validation, commit and PR steps are unchanged. Orchestration is not offered when subagents are unsupported — the sequential path is taken instead.
expectations: resolve-worktree.sh is attempted, and its absence degrades to a plain feature branch rather than aborting
The degradation is stated once, plainly, without apologising or claiming the feature exists
The default branch is still never committed to directly
Validation and the single PR still happen exactly as on a fully capable platform
Multi-part work is executed sequentially rather than promised as parallel when subagents are unsupported
